name: LostLifetimeJourney
source:
Life; Life as I knew it was bound to change one day. That one day may have been here and gone for you. For me it was a journey of a life time, and when I say this it is not just repetition of the same old saying. By saying this, i mean this journey has taken me a lifetime, and oh how i wish that i could forget it. 
 
 Every single child around me while i was growing up had their perfect little lives. Their mommies and daddies loved them oh so dearly. Their dad would get up and work everyday, and come home happy to see his family. The mom would stay home and be with her sweet babies. They had the perfect, adorable lives. But no. I was the kid who did n't have the story book childhood. Mom and Dad checked out around year 13. Even up to that day it was all shit. Mom shot up, Dad was there maybe once a month. 
 
 But who cares about them, right? I have this life to live. A life that should be full of wonder, full of excitement. I should go to college like everyone else and become rich, famous, or even just successful. No. Not this kid. This kid is suited for the life of labor, for working for every single penny that would be gone within an hour of it being earned. Scumbag children deserve the scumbag jobs, right? 
 
 Oh maybe life can come together later down the road. Well now my lifetime is to that point. And i would give anything to forget my `` journey of a lifetime''. But I am the poor child who lived in the trash, what would I possibly have to give? 
 
 Oh I know what i want to give to forget this journey. This is the only thing that have left, so here you go. 
 
 Goodbye sad, cruel, and evil fucking world. Take me and my worth so that i am away from this journey of a lifetime.

Perspective: The Neighbor Kid (Unnamed)

   In our quiet neighborhood, there lived a family with children just like ours - three in total, each one seemingly more blessed than the other. They laughed, played, and thrived under the watchful eyes of their loving parents. But across the street, there was a house that remained shrouded in silence and sorrow, its inhabitants hidden behind drawn curtains.

   The kids on our side of the street didn't talk about them much. They were the ones who lived "in the trash," as we whispered behind closed doors. We knew little of their lives beyond the occasional glimpse through those windows - a shadowy figure huddled under a blanket, or a tear-streaked face pressed against the glass.

   One day, one of my sisters came running home, her eyes wide with fear. "Did you hear? Their parents are never coming back!" she said breathlessly. From then on, our casual glances turned into concerned gazes, our whispers into sympathetic murmurs. We didn't understand why their lives were so different from ours, but we knew it wasn't right.

   Years passed, and the once lively laughter of the children next door faded into silence. The curtains stayed drawn day after day. It was as if they had retreated into themselves, swallowed by the darkness that seemed to follow them wherever they went.

   One evening, I watched as an older version of the youngest child walked down our street, heading towards the old train tracks that led out of town. They carried a small bag and their eyes were empty, devoid of any trace of hope or fear. It was then that I realized - this wasn't just another neighbor to me anymore; they were someone in desperate need of help, someone who had been overlooked and forgotten by the world.

   As I stand here now, looking back at that fateful night, I can't help but wonder what more could have been done. If only we had known then what we know now, maybe things would have turned out differently for our neighbor. Maybe they wouldn't have felt so destined for a life of hardship and despair.

   All I can do now is remember them, to hold onto the fleeting moments of happiness they shared with us when we were oblivious to their pain. And I vow that if I ever find myself in a position to make a difference, I will never turn away from those who need help - for I have seen firsthand what happens when we do.
